words.ex: Small clubs began to coalesce into one large student movement.

words.def: to spread information widely
words.ex: The health department used posters to disseminate safety tips.

words.def: done quickly and without attention to detail
words.ex: A cursory glance at the essay missed several spelling errors.

words.def: deserving blame for something wrong
words.ex: The report found the driver culpable for the crash.

words.def: shockingly obvious and bold, usually about breaking a rule
words.ex: The referee called a flagrant foul.

words.def: extremely bad in a way that stands out
words.ex: Forgetting the bride's name was an egregious mistake.

words.def: far too high in price or amount
words.ex: The stadium charged an exorbitant price for a bottle of water.

words.def: perfect; without any flaws
words.ex: Her manners at the formal dinner were impeccable.

words.def: showing good judgment and sense
words.ex: A judicious use of humor kept the speech lively.

words.def: so strong or obvious it can almost be felt or touched
words.ex: The tension in the room was palpable before the results were read.

words.def: more important than anything else
words.ex: Safety is paramount on a field trip.

words.def: harmful in a slow, quiet way that is hard to notice
words.ex: Lack of sleep has an insidious effect on your mood.

words.def: to move someone or something to a lower or less important position
words.ex: The coach decided to relegate the injured player to the bench.

words.def: to refuse to accept or be connected with something
words.ex: The club chose to repudiate the mean posts made in its name.

words.def: very weak, thin or slight
words.ex: The link between the two stories was tenuous at best.

words.def: to take a position or power by force or without the right to it
words.ex: The jealous duke plotted to usurp the throne.

words.def: to keep changing your mind between choices
words.ex: I vacillate between pizza and tacos every Friday.

words.def: to describe someone as wicked or evil, often unfairly
words.ex: The rival's posters tried to vilify the candidate as a cruel and dangerous liar.

words.def: to weaken or overturn an established system or idea
words.ex: The plot twist was designed to subvert the reader's expectations.

words.def: a natural tendency to behave in a certain way
words.ex: My dog has a propensity for chewing shoes.
